rows.ARS:
Dark red Large-Flowered Climber.
Registration name: KORlabriax
Exhibition name: Amadeus ™
rows.Origin:
Bred by W. Kordes & Sons (Germany, 2003).
Introduced in Canada by Palatine Fruit & Roses in 2007 as 'Amadeus'.
Introduced in United States by Wayside Gardens in 2008 as 'Amadeus'.
rows.Bloom: Red. Mild fragrance. Average diameter 3.25". Medium, double (17-25 petals), cluster-flowered, in small clusters bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Tall, bushy, climbing. Large, glossy, dark green foliage.

Height: 6'7" to 8'2" (200 to 250cm). Width: 39" to 43" (100 to 110cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 6b through 9b (default). Can be used for cut flower, garden, landscape or pillar. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant, very blackspot resistant., very mildew resistant. Remove spent blooms to encourage re-bloom. Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood.. Remove unproductive wood every third year or so.
rows.Notes:
novelty in the range of climing roses with very healthy foliage, captivating by ist large-sized, doubled and shining red flowers
This variety has been decorated with awards (Gold Medal) in international rose competitions.
